$comment: Høst: operators in Swift. The grammar's operator rule leaves every operator as keyword.operator.custom.infix.swift, = included, so the theme could not tell + from =. The operators that compute get their own scopes here and so the structure colour, while = keeps the text colour. Swift requires whitespace on both sides of a binary operator (or on neither), so a binary operator is matched only between whitespace; that keeps < and > in Array<Int> and T: Legeme> as generics, and & in &x as inout. A prefix operator (-x, !x, ~x) is matched before a name, a number, a bracket or a dot. ? and ! as optional marks, ... and ..< as ranges, -> and the ternary ? : are left alone. Applies outside strings and comments, so operators inside \( ) in a string keep the string colour.
